Problem: Coordinates swapped
Context: repo=stm32h735g-dk-bsp, mcu_series=H7, board=None, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=other, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=open, issue_number=5
Root cause: Hi, First, thank you for you prompt responses for the previous issues.
Fix: Hi, First, thank you for you prompt responses for the previous issues.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, medium, MB1520-H735I-B02, MB1520-H735I-C02, MB1520-H735I-C03, TS_SWAP_XY, TS_SWAP_NONE

Technical details:
Hi, First, thank you for you prompt responses for the previous issues. They seem to work great! We have our proprietary app which we have build years ago. This app seems to work fine on the MB1520-H735I-B02 and MB1520-H735I-C02 but it does not work properly on the MB1520-H735I-C03. The problem is that both MB1520-H735I-B02 and MB1520-H735I-C02 require "hTS.Orientation = TS_SWAP_XY;" in order for the touches to work properly but for the board MB1520-H735I-C03 it requires "hTS.Orientation = TS_SWAP_NONE;" in order for the touches to work properly. Why that might be? These lines can be found in STm32TouchController::init() in STM32TouchController.cpp I know that both MB1520-H735I-B02 and MB1520-H735I-C02 use the FT5336_Probe driver and the MB1520-H735I-C03 uses GT911_Probe driver. Could this be the cause? It would be great if we MB1520-H735I-C03 would behave the same as MB1520-H735I-B02 and MB1520-H735I-C02 by requiring for the orientation to be also swapped for x and y, because right now our code could target any of these boards and I would prefer for compile 2 versions of the app one targeted for the MB1520-H735I-B02 and MB1520-H735I-C02 board and another targeted for the MB1520-H735I-C03 😢 In order to support all 3 boards, I would have to compile a version of the app with "hTS.Orientation = TS_SWAP_XY;" for the boards MB1520-H735I-B02 and MB1520-H735I-C02 and then another version of the app with "hTS.Orientation = TS_SWAP_NONE;" for the board MB1520-H735I-C03. This would be a logistics nightmare. Thank you!

Context: repo=stm32h735g-dk-bsp, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H735G, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=3

Fix: Hi, I uploaded the latest example project for STM32H735G-DK, specifically the BSP example.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H735G, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, bsp, STM32H735G-DK, USER, LCD, DEMO3

Technical details:
Hi, I uploaded the latest example project for STM32H735G-DK, specifically the BSP example. The BSP example cycles through multiple demos using the "USER" button. The first demo is an "LCD demo example" showing multiple objects on the screen. The second, third, and fourth are touch examples where we can touch the screen to interact. Everything seems to work at first glance, but using the STM32H735G-DK C03 version, once we get to the fourth example (the touchscreen DEMO3) it systematically goes into HardFault() and the screen freezes. Using a STM32H735G-DK C02 version or B02 version, do not have this problem with the same example. It feels like it might be a driver problem with the new gt911 driver for the touchscreen. The older version they were using the ft5336 driver. Maybe I am wrong. Could you confirm this behaviour with a C03 version? Thank you! P.S. I also have my code that works very well with the B02 and C02 versions, but with C03, once I touch the screen, it instantly freezes. That is when I went to explore more with the Example code provided by ST and discovered this.

Key comments:
Hi, I would like to provide additional details following my previous message. As mentioned earlier, we have a custom application that works correctly on STM32H735G-DK B02 and C02 boards. While debugging on the C03 version, I noticed a key difference during touchscreen initialization: - On B02/C02 boards, BSP_TS_Init() initializes the FT5336 driver - On C03 boards, it initializes the GT911 driver From the BSP code: if (GT911_Probe(Instance) != BSP_ERROR_NONE) { Ts_Driver_Type = FT5336_TS_CTRL; if (FT5336_Probe(Instance) != BSP_ERROR_NONE) { ret = BSP_ERROR_NO_INIT; } } **Behavior in Custom Application** In our application (using TouchGFX), the behavior differs from the BSP demo: - The system does NOT HardFault() on C03 - Touch input is correctly detected Specifically: - sampleTouch() is called as expected - TouchDetected is set correctly - X/Y coordinates are accurate - The function returns true bool STM32TouchController::sampleTouch(int32_t& x, int32_t& y) { TS_State_t TS_State = { 0 }; if (BSP_TS_GetState(0, &TS_State) != BSP_ERROR_NONE) { configASSERT(0); } if (TS_State.TouchDetected)

Problem: BSP OSPI drive using the ISS66WVH8M8 external RAM
Context: repo=stm32h735g-dk-bsp, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H735G, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=low, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=2
Root cause: Hello @alexachso, Thank you for the report.
Fix: Hi, sorry for bothering.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H735G, HAL, usage_question, low, question, bsp, STM32H735G-DK, ISS66WVH8M8, DOM, BOM, CYPRESS-S70KL1281DABHI023

Technical details:
Hi, sorry for bothering. Can someone point me in the right direction? The STM32H735G-DK board changed its layout in version C03 to use the chip ISS66WVH8M8 instead of the original one that was S70KL1281 for HyperRam. In the DOM readme file it is stated: "======================== * 3.0 - 20-November-2024 ======================== + Add C03 BOM with new part references: - U7 (HyperRAM) CYPRESS-S70KL1281DABHI023 replaced with new Memory ISSI_IS66WVH16M8DBLL-100B1LI with impact on firmware. - Several part references updated due to obsolescence (such as transistors or others)." I searched all over github and could not find an example of the stm32h735g_discovery_ospi.c and .h to use the driver for ISS66WVH8M8 instead of using the driver for S70KL1281. I did find other boards in the STM32 family that use this new ISS66WVH8M8 in their ospi HAL driver, but they were setting the HyperRam to different clock speeds than the STM32H735G-DK is doing with S70KL1281. "U7 (HyperRAM) CYPRESS-S70KL1281DABHI023 replaced with new Memory ISSI_IS66WVH16M8DBLL-100B1LI with impact on firmware." -> Where can I find more documentation about the "impact on firmware"? Or maybe there is already a stm32h735g_discovery_ospi.c and .h that implement the driver for ISS66WVH8M8. I could not find either a STM example to load to this board. I was wondering how one could buy the STM32H735G-DK C03 version and upload an existing example. Because all examples use the S70KL1281, they will not work on the C03 version. Thank you!

Key comments:
Hello @alexachso, Thank you for the report. Regarding your question, I have checked with our team, and it seems there is no impact on the firmware. There is a BSP example under the path Projects\STM32H735G-DK\Examples\BSP within the package from [st.com](https://www.st.com/content/st_com/en.html), which can be tested on board version C03. Hi @KRASTM , Thank you! I went and downloaded the latest example for this board, and indeed it works. I then proceeded to compare the files between the example and my project, and all my BSP drivers were not up to date.
